raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not chase fancy things. I farm the way that keeps the land producing and keeps some cash in hand. On my 12 mu, I will still keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for us. Cotton can make money in a good year, but it needs more watching and more spraying, so I will not put too much land into it. This year I will keep 8 mu in wheat followed by summer maize, and 4 mu in cotton.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like we always do, after I clean the field and turn the soil once. I will use ordinary local seed, not expensive seed. Before sowing I will put a base fertilizer, a bit heavier than nothing but not too much because fertilizer costs money. If the wheat looks weak after winter, I will topdress once at jointing. Since we have well water, I will irrigate around the usual times: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around jointing, and once around filling if spring is dry. After wheat harvest in June, the time is tight, so on those same 8 mu I will quickly plant summer maize with simple field preparation, not too much tillage. Maize grows fast, so I will give it one base dressing and one topdressing, and irrigate once if summer rain is not enough. Cotton I will keep on 4 mu only. Cotton needs more labor and more medicine, but it still brings cash, so I keep some. I will plant in April, use what seed is easy to buy locally, put fertilizer in two times, irrigate when it stays dry, and spray only when insects really show up, because every bottle costs money.
